title: Draft State
definition: The term used by Immer to describe the Proxy object you interact with inside an RTK reducer. It represents the 'in-progress' changes before they become the final immutable state.
simpleExplanation: A temporary scratchpad. Inside `createSlice`, the `state` variable passed into your reducer is not the REAL state. It is a 'Draft'. You can scribble all over the draft, and when the function ends, Immer prints a final, clean copy based on your scribbles.

basic: Can you `console.log(state)` directly inside an RTK reducer to see your data?
intermediate: How do you properly log the Draft State in RTK so you can read it?

answers.question: Console log directly?
answers.answer: No! If you `console.log(state)`, you will see a massive, unreadable `Proxy` object, not your actual data.

answers.question: How to log properly?
answers.answer: RTK provides a utility called `current()`. You must import it and log `console.log(current(state))` to read the plain data.
